We should discuss how to specify the BPOs in EL genesis:

Cross-Posting from ACD:
``` 
We are having a long discussion on how to specify the BPO parameters in the genesis configuration in a thread in #interop.
I would like to pull out the discussion from there to here to get more input and it would be good to make a decision on monday.
There are as I see it two ways of specifying the BPOs on the EL.
You can either specify them as normal hardforks or you can specify them in a new special format.

What follows is my opinion on this topic:
I think we should specify them as normal hardforks.

The benefit of a new special format is that we can specify 10/50/100 bpos on a chain, while specifying them as normal hardforks limits us to a predifined number of forks (currently 5).
I doubt that there are cases where it would be important to specify more than 5 BPOs on a chain, and we could update that number pretty quickly.

Adding a new format would create another source of bugs where we have essentially hardforks but specified in a different format.
BPOs require a client release anyway since this is the only true and tested way that we have ever updated the chain.
Users know how to download a new release, they don't know how to specify new command line parameters or update a chain config.

Since BPOs are hardforks, we also need to update the forkid in order to distinguish between updated and non-updated nodes on the network.
So the new mechanism would also need to be able to update the forkid, which again creates another source of potential bugs.

If we specify them as normal hardforks, we can also use our existing testing infrastructure for hardforks instead of needing to write new custom build code.

All in all, I feel the benefit of scheduling arbitrary many BPOs without updating the client does not outweigh the cost and risks.
Especially since this proposal benefits solely the testing teams that want to schedule more than X BPOs. 
We can always update X if we feel that testing teams need more BPOs to work with (which I doubt).
```
